NRecordRowBound's tail stops being Option(Int) and becomes RecordRowTail =
RowClosed | RowContinues(Int) | RowAssumed. The open-closed writer proves
its remainder — the other side is closed, so the residual is exactly what
is left — and marks RowClosed. The open-open writer has seen two partial
sets and their union, never the whole, and marks RowAssumed. The mark rides
the write because the fields alone cannot say which of the two produced
them, and a proof and a guess returning the same field offset is where the
wrong-slot class lives.

Option(Int) already answered whether the chain continues. The missing
question is a different one, and folding both into one shape is what made
open_record_full_fields read a carried union as a closed set.

The reader is deliberately unchanged: RowAssumed answers exactly as
RowClosed. Refusing there turns mn-findtag into a trap — measured twice,
once through the linked tail and once through a bind that recorded nothing
— so the arm is written out rather than merged, and the day it changes is a
day someone chose. What an assumed remainder should do is the open half of
Hbeta.infer.record-row-residual-is-learned-or-assumed and stays the fork.

mentl/9f683de:
Closes layer 9 surfaced after layer 8 band-aid. The wheel's fold,
any, all, count, find use inline anonymous handle-expressions with
state: `handle BODY with FIELD = INIT [, ...] { ARMS }`. Pre-
substrate the seed's parse_primary had NO arm for THandle (kind 7);
the keyword fell through to "treat as unit", producing malformed
AST and unbound state-field varrefs ($acc undefined-global emit).

Substrate:
- bootstrap/src/parser_expr.wat parse_primary: new THandle arm.
  Contextual disambiguation — handle-expr requires `{` follow;
  bare `handle` followed by anything else (TComma, TRParen, TPlus)
  is the wheel's variable-name use (graph.mn handler-arm-args
  graph_chase(handle), chase_node body refs). Lexer always
  tokenizes `handle` as kind 7; parser distinguishes contextually
  via TLBrace peek. Without this guard, parse_handle_expr fires
  on every `handle` identifier reference, inducing infinite parse
  loop (perm_alloc trap on wheel-prefix at graph.mn).

- bootstrap/src/parser_handler.wat new $parse_handle_expr:
  parses `handle BODY [with state] [{ arms }]`. Reuses parse_block
  for body, parse_handler_state for optional state, parse_handler_arms
  for optional arms. Builds HandleExpr AST [tag=93][body][arms][state]
  — extends prior 12-byte shape additively (offset 12 state).
  Gracefully handles no-arms-block form (handle BODY with HANDLER)
  for productive-under-error.

- bootstrap/src/lower/walk_handle.wat $lower_handle: reads state
  from offset 12; threads through $lower_handler_arms_as_decls so
  state-field names bind in outer scope per layer-7 capture
  substrate. Inline state-bearing handle-exprs now produce LUpval
  arm-body references for state-field captures (LFn body reads
  __state[8+4*slot] at runtime).

Bug-fix uncovered:
- bootstrap/src/infer/walk_expr.wat walk_expr_handle_arm_iter:
  pre-existing bug at line 463 — read arm.body via raw byte offset
  4 instead of $record_get(arm, 1). Records are
  [tag:i32][arity:i32][fields...] (record.wat:22)
